title_as_printed: Differentiation of Subjective Cognitive Decline, Mild Cognitive Impairment, and Dementia Using qEEG/ERP-Based Cognitive Testing and Volumetric MRI in an Outpatient Specialty Memory Clinic

blind_codes.Task_Type: T3 (three-class SCD/MCI/dementia with AUC; T1 arguable via MCI-vs-SCD pairwise AUC)
blind_codes.Validation_Type: V2 (LOOCV on n = 161 and n = 111, above V1's <100; V1 arguable)

registry_codes.Sample_N_Approx: 161 — 69 SCD / 53 MCI / 39 dementia (subset of 111 with vMRI)

Task_Type.reason: Two readings. T3 (preferred): the primary model is a three-class multinomial logistic regression (SCD vs MCI vs dementia) scored by AUC, i.e. multi-class staging. T1 (registry): the paper also reports pairwise AUC, sensitivity and specificity for MCI versus SCD (Table 3; combined model AUC 0.79, 95% CI 0.69-0.90) and stresses the SCD-MCI distinction as its clinical contribution. SCD participants are objectively unimpaired (mean MMSE 28.7), so the MCI-vs-SCD contrast works as MCI-vs-unimpaired discrimination, although the paper states it 'does not include a healthy control group' (p.7).
Task_Type.quote: However, the combined qEEG/ERP and vMRI model was able to distinguish between the two stages with a relatively high degree of accuracy. In routine clinical care, this model may be an important adjunct to traditional assessments in distinguishing between SCD and MCI

Category.reason: The data domains of the predictors are qEEG/ERP (electrophysiology, C2) and automated volumetric MRI (neuroimaging, C1). The registry's C5 omits both primary domains. The clinical data (chart review, MMSE, demographics) supplies only the diagnostic labels and covariates.
Category.quote: We investigated diagnostic categorization using an FDA-cleared quantitative electroencephalographic/event-related potential (qEEG/ERP)-based cognitive testing system (eVox® by Evoke Neuroscience) combined with an automated volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (vMRI) tool (Neuroreader® by Brainreader).

Validation_Type.reason: LOOCV within the same clinic sample, with no separate test set. V1 is defined for LOOCV with n < 100, and here n = 161 (qEEG) and n = 111 (qEEG+vMRI), so V2 fits.
Validation_Type.quote: Due to the relatively small size of our sample, we used leave-one-out cross-validation to provide an unbiased assessment of the model without splitting the available data into training and validation data sets.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 161 with qEEG/ERP (69 SCD + 53 MCI + 39 dementia); the vMRI subset is 111.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: Of 161 patients with qEEG/ERP data, 69 were categorized with SCD, 53 with MCI, and 39 with dementia due to AD

Publication_Year.reason: Journal of Alzheimer's Disease 90 (2022); pre-press 11 November 2022.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Retrospective chart review at a single outpatient memory clinic (Pacific Brain Health Center); ADNI is not used.

notes: Category error affects the research-domain census: the study is counted as clinical (C5) rather than as electrophysiology plus neuroimaging.
